newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Chevron PNG natgas pipeline layers line up.
newsitem.headline: Chevron PNG natgas pipeline layers line up.

text.p: Firm proposals from up to eight international companies to build a A$2 billion Papua New Guinea (PNG) to Australia gas pipeline will be submitted on Monday, pipeline project manager, Chevron Corp said on Friday.
"The consortiums are of high quality. I cannot reveal their names but there are no surprises in there," Chevron project manager, John Powell told an oil and gas conference.

Powell also said international tenders had been called for the 700,000 tonnes of hardened steel necessary for the pipeline "as no one country, including Japan, can supply that amount of steel with the necessary diameter," Powell said.
The Southern Pacific Pipeline Co, as it has been named by Chevron, is aiming to deliver gas from the Kutubu gas field in the Southern Highlands of PNG to northern Queensland by 2001.
The pipeline consortium also includes PNG's Orogen Minerals Ltd and Oil Search Ltd, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd.
Chevron earlier this month said it hoped to announce a pipeline construction winner by the end of next month and announce a pipeline company had joined the consortium by October 1.

Supply tenders for the steel to be used for the pipeline would most likely be won by mills in Taiwan and South Korea who had the equipment to build pipe diameters of up to 750 mm (30 inches), Powell told Reuters after the conference.
Powell said earlier the biggest challenge the Chevron consortium faced was ensuring the process of getting the PNG, Australian and Queensland government approvals co-ordinated.
Powell said reported criticism of the project from PNG candidates during the run-up to this month's PNG election would disippate in a post-election atmosphere.
"It will be up to us to convince the PNG government. Our view is that there will be considerable value to both countries," Powell said.
The Queensland government had already expressed its support for the project while the Federal government regarded the pipeline as "the number one priority in Australia," Powell said.

Earlier this month, Chevron and Australian aluminium group, Comalco Ltd said they would jointly study the potential of extending the pipeline to the Queensland town of Gladstone, one of Comalco's preferred sites for an alumina refinery.
"Comalco tells us they need gas by 2001. All necessary (government) approvals need to be in place by September, 1998," Powell said.
